# bugs #3200: DIE references in .debug_info are one byte too high after a source path with a backslash escape

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3200/
- Category: [Already fixed in trunk](../../fixed-upstream.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Close as fixed in r12964, the fix for bug #3303. r12536 fixed the end-of-siblings markers.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The ticket reports two defects in the `.debug_info` section of an stm8 ELF file. `readelf` rejects
end-of-siblings markers, and DIEs refer to an abbreviation 117 that does not exist. A maintainer
fixed the markers in r12536 and could not reproduce the abbreviation error.

The `firmware.elf` of the last comment, from SDCC 4.1.12 #12697, shows the cause of the
abbreviation error. `readelf -wi` reports that error for it and no end-of-siblings marker. In the
compile unit of `stm8s_gpio.c`, each of the 45 `DW_AT_type` and `DW_AT_sibling` values is one
higher than the offset of the DIE that it refers to. The name of that unit is a Windows path with
the directory `packages\framework-ststm8spl`, and the file holds one form feed byte in place of
the characters `\f`. The name of the unit of `src\main.c` has no such sequence, and its 7
references are correct. Abbreviation 117 is the letter `u` of `unsigned char`, the second byte of
the DIE of that base type.

On r17176 a program of two files was compiled for stm8 with `--debug --out-fmt-elf
--opt-code-size` and linked. It has the struct of the ticket's excerpt, with five `volatile`
bytes, and functions that take a pointer to it. The test ran on Linux with file names that contain
backslashes, among them `\f` and `\n`, and again with plain names. `readelf` reports no warning
for `.debug_info` or for the other debug sections. Every reference is the offset of a DIE, and
`DW_AT_name` holds the path with its backslashes. The sources of the ticket's project are not
attached and were not used. stm8-gdb and a Windows host were not tested.

## Fixed by

[r12964](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/12964/), the fix for bug #3303. Before it,
`dwWriteString` in `src/SDCCdwarf2.c` wrote the string into an `.ascii` line unchanged, and the
assembler read a backslash and the character after it as one escape sequence. The size that the
compiler computes for a DIE counts `strlen` of the string plus one. Each such sequence therefore
placed the DIEs after it one byte below the offsets in the references. Since r12964,
`dwWriteString` escapes the string with `string_escape`. The reporter's last test used a snapshot
of r12697, which is older.

[r12536](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/12536/) fixed the markers, as a maintainer's comment
says. Before it, `dwWriteTags` wrote end-of-siblings markers for the root DIE, which has no
siblings.

## Related

Bug #3303 reports the damage to the path strings themselves.
